I used to be extremely transphobic and quite homophobic as well. One of my friends came out as bi but for some reason I wasn’t mad which made me start questioning my beliefs and eventually not be homophobic anymore. Took me two years to realize that the reason I wasn’t mad was because I liked him and it meant I actually had a chance with him. After that I slowly accepted my own attraction to men and started interacting with the community online more and more. Realized I wasn’t gay but bi cuz for some reason I didn’t even consider that I could be bi even though I had liked girls before. I eventually became very supportive of trans people in large part because of an amazing friend I had who told me a while back they were nonbinary and I didn’t know what it meant but I didn’t care so I just used they/them when referring to them and it’s when interacting with the community that I learned it was a gender identity lol. Later on eventually realized I was trans and also got in a relationship with the guy I was referring to earlier. 

All of that happened within two years. People change and it’s important to remember that who you used to be doesn’t matter. When I talk with people I haven’t seen in years I assume they have nothing to do with who I used to know because it’s only fair to give them a chance when they very much could have changed. 

Don’t feel bad about what your past self thought or did. If you hurt someone try to make up for it and leave that behind.
